title: Watch {name} at work: short videos of real tasks · {name}
description: Short videos of {name} at work: a spreadsheet answered, a letter written, an email sent only once you agree. In your language, with sound.
h1: See {name} at work, in a minute.
lede: Each video is {name} itself, playing real tasks again in your language, by day or by night. Pause it, go back, slow it down, or turn the sound off.
more.title: More to watch
more.why: Less than a minute each: what a spreadsheet becomes, what {name} asks before it acts, and a first request.
how.title: Watch it your way
how.why: None of it is a recording: it is {name}, playing a task again, so it speaks your language and fits your screen.
end.title: Your turn.
end.why: {name} is free, open source, and runs in a browser tab: nothing to install, no account to make.
minutes.ask: Send these minutes to the team.
minutes.subject: Minutes, 24 October
minutes.answer: Sent to the team, with the minutes attached.
jean.title: {name} in a minute
jean.about: What {name} is, for anyone who has used ChatGPT: the AI you like, a file in and something made back, and everything kept on your device.
jean.chart.say.ask: Drop in a spreadsheet and ask, in your own words.
jean.chart.say.program: The sums are worked out by a program, in a sandbox in your browser. Not guessed.
jean.chart.say.made: And back comes what you asked for, made.
jean.letter.ask: Help me write to my landlord about the damp in the bedroom. Firm, but polite.
jean.letter.answer:
Here’s a draft:

“Dear Mr Martin,

Since early October, the bedroom wall has been damp and the paint is peeling. Could you send someone to look at it this month?

Kind regards,”
jean.letter.say.any: Use GPT, Claude, Gemini, or an AI on your own computer.
jean.letter.say.where: Each answer says which AI wrote it: here, the one on this computer.
jean.minutes.say.asks: Before it sends, shares or deletes anything, {name} asks you.
jean.keep.title: Keep everything.
jean.keep.facts: Your history, files and memory stay on your device.
As plain files, in one backup you can take anywhere.
jean.end.title: Your turn.
jean.end.line: Nothing to install, no account to make.
spreadsheet.title: A spreadsheet, answered
spreadsheet.about: For anyone who works in Excel: a question in plain words, the figures worked out by a program, and a chart back.
spreadsheet.open.title: A spreadsheet, answered.
spreadsheet.open.line: A year of sales, and one question.
spreadsheet.task.say.file: You drop in the file: {months} months of sales, {products} products.
spreadsheet.task.say.ask: Then you ask in your own words. No formula to write.
spreadsheet.task.say.brain: Your request and the file go to the AI you chose, and nowhere else.
spreadsheet.task.say.program: For the figures, it writes a small program that runs in a sandbox in your browser.
spreadsheet.task.say.chart: What you asked for comes back made: here, a chart.
spreadsheet.task.say.data: The figures behind it are one click away.
spreadsheet.task.say.read: Under each answer: what was read to write it.
spreadsheet.end.title: Your turn.
spreadsheet.end.line: Try it with our sample spreadsheet, or your own.
asks-first.title: {name} asks first
asks-first.about: What {name} does on its own, and what it asks you before doing: sending, sharing, deleting, anything outside.
asks-first.open.title: {name} asks first.
asks-first.task.say.ask: Here, a request that sends something: the minutes, to the team.
asks-first.task.say.card: Sending is something {name} asks about first: you see what goes, and where.
asks-first.task.say.allow: Allow it once, and it goes.
asks-first.rules.title: You decide.
asks-first.rules.facts: Its own files: it reads and writes them.
Sending, sharing, deleting: it asks you first.
first-task.title: Your first task
first-task.about: A first request to {name}, in everyday words, and what comes back.
first-task.open.title: Your first task.
first-task.open.line: Ask as you would ask a person.
first-task.task.ask: Write a short thank-you note to my neighbour Sam, who watered my plants while I was away.
first-task.task.answer:
Dear Sam,

Thank you so much for watering my plants while I was away. I came back to a balcony in full bloom, and I know that took time and care.

If you’re ever away yourself, I’d be glad to return the favour.

With thanks,
first-task.task.say.ask: Say what you need, in your own words.
first-task.task.say.brain: It goes to the AI you chose, which writes back as it thinks.
first-task.task.say.aloud: Have it read aloud, or ask for a change in your own words.
first-task.end.title: Nothing to install.
